messages:
anya (cust-succ): heads-up: urgent from ACME — their Dedicated pool dp-05 suddenly dropped throughput and started returning 429s + big latency spikes around 10:12UTC. customer impact: chat timeouts.
mike (eng-runtime): @anya can you paste a couple request ids and any stack traces? 429 could be ingress ratecap or internal throttling. also did they change client batching?
anya (cust-succ): req ids: req-897, req-901, req-908. customer logs show errors like "rate_limit_exceeded" and intermittent 502s. p50 jumped from ~120ms to ~2s. :grimacing:
jen (support): escalated, they're very frustrated. will cc billing in case they try retries and blow credits.
deploy-bot: deploy dp-05 autoscaler v1.4.2 started at 2026-03-17T09:58:32Z
rob (sre): looking at host metrics — GPU util is fine, but inference queue length is up and the runtime packer shows many tiny dispatch windows (avg pack size ~2). lots of tiny windows -> high dispatch overhead.
mike (eng-runtime): tiny windows = token-choke pattern. The continuous packer is dispatching lots of small jobs so kernel startup/warp underutilization kills throughput. what's scheduler quantum and max_batch tokens on dp-05?
kevin (infra): dp-05 config: scheduler_quantum=8ms, max_batch_tokens=4096, max_batch_size=8. autoscaler added 2 nodes at 10:05UTC.
mike (eng-runtime): hypothesis: client release caused an influx of short-turn chat messages (4-12 tokens) so packs are fragmenting. autoscaler added capacity but packing inefficiency means throughput didn't recover.
anya (cust-succ): confirmed — they rolled a chat client update that splits messages into many tiny inference calls. they didn't change any Redwood config.
rob (sre): quick repro steps I ran from staging: hit dp-05 with 5k concurrent short (6 token) requests. observed packer stats: dispatch rate high, avg pack size 1.9, kernel occupancy low, token throughput down ~66%. errors spike during peak.
jen (support): what mitigation can we offer ACME immediately?
mike (eng-runtime): short-term options: 1) ask customer to batch client-side if possible (coalesce few messages), 2) increase scheduler_quantum (e.g., 8 -> 18ms) so packer waits to aggregate more, improving kernel fill at cost of slight p95 latency increase, 3) enable adaptive small-window hold_time (hold tiny requests for X ms to combine).
kevin (infra): we can canary a quantum bump on dp-05 now. also enabling adaptive hold_time is a config flip but needs rollout validation.
rob (sre): agree canary is lowest risk. I'll bump quantum 8->18ms on one node and run telemetry for 10 minutes. if p95 stays acceptable and throughput improves, widen.
deploy-bot: scaling dp-05 pool +2 nodes (requested by rob)
anya (cust-succ): told customer we're doing a canary and will follow-up in 15m. they asked for an ETA to full fix.
mike (eng-runtime): note: long-term we should add runtime detection for high tiny-window rate and an autoscale/packing policy that adjusts hold_time/quantum automatically. also document SDK guidance for short-chat workloads.
rob (sre): canary results after 8m: p95 latency dropped from ~2.1s -> 520ms, throughput increased ~3.4x, avg pack size went 2 -> 11, 429 errors cleared.
jen (support): customer confirms improved responsiveness, very relieved. asking for permanent tuning and SDK best-practices.
kevin (infra): action: I'll add an infra ticket to implement adaptive_hold_time and schedule config rollout next week.
mike (eng-runtime): action: I'll draft SDK guidance for batching short messages and an internal RFC for adaptive quantum/hold_time heuristics.
anya (cust-succ): thanks all — I'll close the customer loop and file the postmortem. will re-open if regression. :white_check_mark:
